name: Crucible Industries Viper Mk.III 'Copperhead'
description:
The Crucible Industries Viper Mk.III is a compact semi-automatic pistol chambered in 10mm Auto, designed for operators who need maximum stopping power in a concealable package. The frame uses Crucible's proprietary recoil-dampening polymer matrix that reduces felt recoil by roughly thirty percent compared to conventional frames in the same caliber. The barrel is chrome-lined and rated for +P ammunition.

The Copperhead is a violent little gun. The 10mm Auto round delivers significantly more energy than standard pistol calibers, and the Viper III's compact dimensions concentrate that violence into a package barely larger than a subcompact 9mm. The trade-off is magazine capacity — eight rounds — and aggressive muzzle blast that announces every shot to everyone within a city block.

Crucible Industries positions the Viper III as a backup weapon for professionals and a primary weapon for individuals who expect their first encounter to be their only warning. The marketing materials feature the tagline 'First Round Decisive' — a polite way of saying the weapon is designed to end confrontations with a single well-placed shot.
specifications: caliber: 10mm Auto effective_range: 40 meters rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 8 rounds weight: 0.72 kg
tactical_use: A high-power compact pistol designed for decisive first-shot engagements. The 10mm Auto round is effective against lightly armored targets and augmented individuals with subdermal plating. Best deployed at close range where the compact frame and aggressive recoil are manageable. Not suitable for sustained firefights due to limited magazine capacity.
cultural_context: The Copperhead has a reputation as a 'serious person's' backup gun. Carrying one implies you've thought carefully about what you might need to shoot and concluded that 9mm isn't enough. In street culture, being described as 'a Copperhead type' means someone who plans for the worst and arms accordingly.
known_users: Experienced the Gray Zone enforcers who saved up
story_hooks: A Copperhead loaded with prototype armor-piercing 10mm rounds is found at a scene where the target should have been unkillable.
Crucible Industries is quietly recalling Viper IIIs with a specific serial range — the recoil-dampening matrix is degrading and the frames are cracking under sustained fire.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutally compact semi-automatic pistol with an aggressive, business-like stance. The Copperhead presents a squared-off profile with a slightly longer barrel than typical subcompacts, giving it a purposeful, predatory appearance. The frame sits low and wide, optimized for recoil management rather than ergonomic comfort.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 17.8 cm | Height: 12.4 cm | Barrel length: 9.1 cm | Width: 3.2 cm across slide
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and bottom-heavy in the hand despite compact dimensions — 0.72 kg distributed to favor a forward grip. Feels denser than its size suggests, with a weighty confidence that communicates serious purpose. The recoil-dampening matrix adds negligible bulk but noticeable heft.
physical_description.primary_material: Frame: Crucible proprietary recoil-dampening polymer matrix (reinforced nanocomposite). Slide: Hardened steel. Barrel: Chrome-lined steel rated for overpressure ammunition.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte gunmetal gray on steel components with a slight satin sheen from the chrome lining visible in the barrel. Polymer frame features a textured, non-reflective charcoal finish with subtle copper-tone accent striping along the grip panels and slide serrations.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Gunmetal gray and charcoal black. Accents: Burnished copper striping on grip and along slide cuts, industrial steel trigger guard.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressive crosshatch polymer texture on front and backstrap, interrupted by inlaid copper-toned grip panels with a finer diamond-pattern grip. Trigger guard features sharp serrations. Trigger face is cold, bare metal with a slightly raised profile.
distinctive_features: Pronounced slide serrations front and rear for positive manipulation
Barrel is visibly chrome-lined with subtle copper toning from manufacturing
Copper-accented grip panels with integrated Crucible Industries logo (Φ motif)
Aggressive muzzle brake cuts on barrel crown visible from side profile
Tactical rail under frame for light/laser attachment
Witness holes on magazine floor plate showing round count
Recessed safety lever integrated into frame — no protrusion
Slightly curved slide profile emphasizing compact but combat-capable aesthetic
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo (stylized Φ symbol) stamped into right grip panel. 'VIPER MK.III COPPERHEAD' and 'Crucible Aquaculture Division' engraved along right side of slide in clean sans-serif font. Serial number stamped on left frame rail. '+P RATED' and '10mm AUTO' marked on barrel near chamber.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-ready and well-maintained — operators who carry the Copperhead take professional care of it. Typically shows light wear on edges and trigger guard from holster contact, microscopic powder residue in muzzle brake cuts, and occasional light carbon fouling on lower receiver. No cosmetic damage; this is a working gun kept in fighting condition.
